name: KOIRA
description: Koira (Finnish for 'Dog') is a traditional Finnish card game for three to eight players. It is an avoidance game belonging to the 'beating' family (like Skitgubbe). The game is famous for its social element: the loser is called the 'Dog' and may be jokingly required to bark. It is played in two distinct phases: a collection phase where card count is expanded, and an avoidance phase where players try to empty their hands.

content.text: Koira (Finnish for 'Dog') is a traditional Finnish card game for three to eight players. It is an avoidance game belonging to the 'beating' family (like Skitgubbe). The game is famous for its social element: the loser is called the 'Dog' and may be jokingly required to bark. It is played in two distinct phases: a collection phase where card count is expanded, and an avoidance phase where players try to empty their hands.

Originates from 19th-century Finnish folk traditions, closely related to the Swedish game Skitgubbe and the Norwegian Mattis. It was historically a common game among forestry workers and farming families.
3 players is the classic competitive format.
Standard 52-card deck. Ace is high, 2 is low.

items.text: Tie: take back and deal: When there is a tie for highest card in phase 1, the tied players take their cards back; the other cards in the trick are arranged in ascending order and dealt one at a time to the tied players as evenly as possible, counterclockwise from the last player who played a tied card.
Trump ends trick: In phase 2, a trump played on a non-trump immediately ends the trick; the player of the trump sets the cards aside and leads to a new trick.

Pick lowest card only: When picking up from a trick, only the lowest card is taken; if the lowest play is a sequence, only the bottom card of that sequence is taken. A sequence counts as in play until all its cards have been removed.
